title: Watermark/Provenance Fragility x Disclosure Mandates: When the Mechanism Can't Support the Rule

original_idea.body:
# Watermark/Provenance Fragility x Disclosure Mandates: When the Mechanism Can't Support the Rule

**Problem:** Governance mandates AI-content provenance; provenance signals are fragile/strippable. Compliant labeled content silently loses provenance downstream.

**Direction:** Apply realistic transformations to a public watermarking method, measure survival rates, map against mandate requirements.

**Why it matters:** Shows transparency rule and mechanism are mismatched. Consumer GPU, open tools.

**Relevant context:** artificialintelligenceact.eu; arXiv:2407.14981.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Vague impact: provenance mostly targets misinformation, not the catastrophic-risk pathways prioritized; chain to catastrophe is weak.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Apply standard transformations to an open watermarking tool and measure survival; guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped robustness experiment with clear survival-rate metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open tools, independent robustness study; weak lab incentive.

low_compute.reasoning: Image/text watermarking on a consumer GPU; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Watermark-robustness attacks are heavily studied already.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Watermark fragility under transformations is well-documented in existing literature.
